Police in Vietnam have rescued more than 400 cats in a bust of a cat meat crime ring in Ho Chi Minh City, according to animal welfare groups and local media reports.

More than 40 cats were reunited with their owners after the multiday operation last week, but several dozen of those rescued have died due to the harsh conditions in which they were found, the groups said.

rfi.title: Ebola death toll in DRC and Uganda passes 200 as funding pledges fall short
rfi.description: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda has claimed more than 200 lives in its first month, according to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. With hundreds more cases confirmed, it is the worst Ebola emergency in years – yet less than 10 percent of pledges ​made to support the fight against ‌the disease have been received from donors.

rfi.title: French court confirms Moroccan footballer Hakimi to stand trial on rape charge
rfi.description: A French appeals court on Friday confirmed that Moroccan football star Achraf Hakimi will face trial over the alleged rape of a woman in 2023, an accusation the Paris Saint-Germain defender denies. The ruling came the same day the Morocco captain was due to lead his national team against Scotland in their second World Cup match.

rfi.title: Iran peace talks put on hold after Vance scraps Swiss visit

rfi.title: Burnham wins key UK poll, paving way for bid to challenge PM Starmer
rfi.description: Veteran UK Labour politician Andy Burnham emphatically won a crunch by-election on Friday, securing a parliamentary seat and clearing the way for a widely expected leadership challenge against beleaguered Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

rfi.title: Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM militants claim deadly attack on Niger airport
rfi.description: West Africa's al-Qaeda affiliate, the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims, has claimed responsibility for an attack on Niger's main airport and a nearby military airbase in the capital Niamey, which the government said killed at least 11 soldiers and two civilians.

rfi.title: Mexico advances to World Cup last 32 to set up final scramble for glory
rfi.description: Co-hosts Mexico beat South Korea 1-0 on Thursday night to claim Group A at the 2026 World Cup – and set up a final round of games that could see South Africa, South Korea and the Czech Republic join them in the knockout stages.

rfi.title: 'Trump is an aberration in US politics', former security adviser tells RFI
rfi.description: Former United States national security adviser John Bolton worked closely with President Donald Trump during his first term in the White House, but is highly critical of the president's current policies regarding Iran. Bolton tells RFI why negotiations to end the Middle East war are likely to fail, and in a prescient move Swiss authorities announced Friday that US-Iran talks planned in Switzerland were "postponed".

rfi.title: EU leaders weigh new trade defences to counter China's export dominance
rfi.description: European Union leaders will debate on Thursday whether the bloc needs stronger trade defences to curb a surge of Chinese exports that Brussels sees as a threat to European industry and jobs.

rfi.title: Paris opens canal to swimmers and SNCF cuts trains, as France faces 40C heatwave
rfi.description: A heatwave extending is expected this week, with temperatures expected to approach 40C. Rail services will be cut to avoid air-conditioning failures and Paris has authorised swimming in the Canal Saint-Martin.

rfi.title: G7 leaders back tougher stance on Russia as Trump shifts line
rfi.description: G7 leaders have backed increased pressure on Russia to end its war in Ukraine, after US President Donald Trump signalled a shift towards a tougher line against Moscow at the group's summit in France.

rfi.title: France among 15 countries to pledge to target illegal fishing with shared data
rfi.description: France is among 15 countries to have signed the Mombasa Declaration, unveiled at the Our Ocean Conference held in the Kenyan port city this week. The global agreement, aimed at combatting illegal and destructive fishing, commits countries to improved data collection and sharing of information on fishing vessels.

rfi.title: Yirenkyi's late flourish starts Ghana's World Cup party in Canada
rfi.description: Caleb Yirenkyi scored his first international goal on Wednesday night to edge Ghana past Panama in their opening game of the 2026 World Cup at the Toronto Stadium.

rfi.title: France grants reparations to children uprooted from Réunion Island
rfi.description: Paris has approved a law granting reparations to more than 2,000 children from Réunion Island who were sent to mainland France between 1962 and 1984 – acknowledging the state's responsibility for a policy that separated families, uprooted minors and left lasting trauma.

rfi.title: Air France permanently closes Mali operation, after flights halted in 2023
rfi.description: Air France has closed all operations in Mali, underlining how air links in the Sahel have been reshaped by strained ties between France and military-led governments, airspace closures, suspended services and recent security concerns around Bamako.

rfi.title: Kane strikes twice as England overpower Croatia 4-2 in Dallas
rfi.description: England skipper Harry Kane scored two goals as his side opened their 2026 World Cup campaign in Texas on Wednesday night, with a 4-2 victory over an initially stubborn Croatia.

rfi.title: Trump heads to Versailles as Macron faces row over lavish reception

rfi.title: France ramps up fight against tiger mosquitoes after record outbreaks
rfi.description: France is bracing for another summer of dengue and chikungunya risk, as climate change helps the disease-carrying tiger mosquito spread north and authorities test new ways to curb its advance.

euronews.title: Estonia creates AI ‘ID Codes’ to govern autonomous agents

lemonde.description: Unique en France, ce site de 28 hectares près de Vierzon sert à la formation des pompiers et d’outil de sensibilisation face à la progression du risque de feux de forêt dans une région de plus en plus exposée aux brasiers en raison du réchauffement climatique.

france24fr.description: Si la Coupe du monde de football essentiellement se joue sur le terrain, l'événement se vit aussi en dehors, et notamment sur les réseaux sociaux. Des vikings norvégiens aux moqueries à l'égard de Cristiano Ronaldo, petit tour d'horizon avec Antoine Besse.

france24fr.title: À Paris, un rassemblement "contre les exécutions politiques en Iran" interdit par la police
france24fr.description: Initialement prévu samedi après-midi à Paris, un rassemblement contre les exécutions d'opposants en Iran a été interdit par la préfecture de police. Dans un arrêté publié jeudi soir, la préfecture invoque un "contexte national et international particulièrement tendu" et un risque d'affrontements pouvant "troubler gravement l'ordre public". Les organisateurs dénoncent une décision "sous des prétextes sans fondement".

france24fr.title: Quand le business des cartes Panini explose avec la Coupe du monde
france24fr.description: Alors que le #Mondial2026 bat son plein, une autre compétition fait rage : la chasse aux vignettes Panini. Au Brésil, des milliers de passionnés se réunissent dans les rues pour compléter leur album et échanger leurs précieux doublons.

france24fr.title: Affaire Lyhanna : Marc Trévidic s’inquiète des défaillances de l’État
france24fr.description: Dans l’émission Avec Judith, Marc Trévidic livre un constat sans concession de l’état de la justice française. Il décrit un système sous tension, fragilisé par un manque chronique de moyens et par ce qu’il considère comme un désengagement de l’État dans la protection de l’enfance. Il revient notamment sur l’affaire Lyhanna, qu’il cite comme révélatrice des tensions et des défaillances du système.

france24fr.title: Un pinceau pour seule arme : qui était l'artiste dissident russe Skrepetski, abattu en Pologne ?
france24fr.description: L'artiste et dissident russe Semion Skrepetski, réputé pour ses caricatures hostiles à Vladimir Poutine et au dirigeant tchétchène Ramzan Kadyrov, a été abattu lundi en Pologne, où il était réfugié depuis 2021. Père de cinq enfants, son assassinat a choqué la société polonaise et accroît l'inquiétude des exilés russes et biélorusses installés dans le pays. Portrait.

france24fr.title: Liban en direct : Israël et le Hezbollah conviennent d'un cessez-le-feu (responsable américain)
Élément Terre à VivaTech : l'IA est-elle compatible avec la lutte contre le changement climatique?
france24fr.description: Élément Terre est au salon VivaTech. Audrey Racine reçoit Vincent Jacamon de l'Agence Internationale de l'Énergie. L'intelligence artificielle est très gourmande en énergie, en eau et en matériels comme les puces électroniques. Cet appétit est-il compatible avec la lutte contre le changement climatique ? Les data centers aussi vont devoir viser la sobriété...

france24fr.title: Élément Terre à VivaTech : adapter les villes au climat futur
france24fr.description: Élément Terre était cette semaine au salon VivaTech. Invitée d'Audrey Racine, Hélène Chartier est directrice de l'urbanisme au C40. Le C40 est une coalition de maires de grandes villes qui se concertent sur les défis du changement climatique pour leurs municipalités. Hélène Chartier nous décrit les changements à apporter dans les modes de vie urbains.

france24fr.title: Soutenir les droits des femmes, c'est préserver la démocratie
france24fr.description:
Le G7 s'est achevé sans que les droits des femmes n'aient été abordés. La raison ? Trop "confrontationnel" selon Emmanuel Macron, qui voulait éviter une crise diplomatique avec l'allié américain Donald Trump. Pourtant le backlash sur les droits des femmes n'a jamais été aussi important. En Hongrie, en Pologne, aux Etats-Unis, c'est d'abord à l'IVG que s'en sont pris les gouvernements.
 
Aux États-Unis, il est désormais plus difficile pour les personnes qui ont changé de nom au cours de leur vie,

france24fr.title: Présidentielle en Colombie : Ivan Cepeda, défenseur des droits humains et des réformes sociales
france24fr.description: Défenseur des victimes d'un conflit armé interne vieux de six décennies, le candidat de gauche Ivan Cepeda promet de poursuivre les réformes sociales amorcées par son compagnon de route Gustavo Petro. Il propose notamment de donner la priorité aux dépenses sociales et à la sortie progressive des énergies fossiles.

france24fr.title: Royaume-Uni : le travailliste Andy Burnham élu député, la bataille s'annonce contre Starmer
france24fr.description: Le principal rival de Keir Starmer au Labour, Andy Burnham, a franchi vendredi une étape cruciale dans son ambition de le remplacer à Downing Street en se faisant élire député lors d'une législative partielle.

france24fr.title: Challenge App Afrique : Cindy Monjoli, lauréate de l'édition 2026
france24fr.description: Cindy Monjoli est la lauréate du Challenge App Afrique. L'édition 2026 de ce concours de start-up, porté par RFI et France 24, avait pour thème la gestion, la transofrmation et la valorisation des déchets.

france24fr.title: Exclusif : à Bunia en RD Congo, les soignants en première ligne face à Ebola
france24fr.description: La République démocratique du Congo est confrontée à une nouvelle vague du virus Ebola. Le bilan est déjà très lourd avec plus de 200 morts en un mois. Les soignants sont en première ligne pour tenter d'endiguer la propagation du virus. Nos équipes ont rencontré des médecins et des infirmiers, qui racontent leur combat quotidien, mais aussi leur désarroi face au manque criant de moyens.

france24fr.title: 🔴En direct : violents combats au Sud-Liban, quatre soldats israéliens tués et 18 morts côté libanais
Le footballeur marocain Achraf Hakimi rattrapé par un procès pour viol en plein Mondial
france24fr.description: La ⁠cour d'appel ​de Versailles a ordonné, vendredi, le ​renvoi d'Achraf Hakimi ​devant ‌la cour criminelle des Yvelines pour viol. L’affaire suit le défenseur du PSG et capitaine de la sélection nationale du Maroc depuis trois ans.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : comment les soignants luttent contre le virus Ebola ?
france24fr.description: Depuis un peu plus d’un mois, la République démocratique du Congo est confrontée à la 17ᵉ épidémie d’Ebola de son histoire. Face à cette nouvelle souche du virus, aucun vaccin n’est encore disponible. Le bilan est déjà très lourd : plus de 200 morts. Nos équipes se sont rendues à Bunia, chef-lieu de la province de l’Ituri et épicentre de l’épidémie. Sur place, médecins et infirmiers racontent leur combat quotidien.

france24fr.title: L'actu en dessin : avec le protocole d'accord, Trump fait faux bon à Israël
france24fr.description: La décision de Donald Trump de valider un protocole d'accord avec l'Iran, incluant un arrêt des hostilités au Liban, est perçu comme un affront par Israël. L'État hébreu a averti qu'il ne retirerait pas ses troupes du pays du Cèdre. Un sujet traité par l'illustrateur Cambon, sous forme de clin d'œil à la Coupe du monde de football, qui bat son plein sur le continent américain.

nzz.description: Der Bundesrat will den Schutzstatus S für Geflüchtete aus der Ukraine voraussichtlich über März 2027 hinaus weiterführen. Zugleich lässt er prüfen, ob wehrpflichtige ukrainische Männer künftig davon ausgeschlossen werden sollen.

nzz.description: Die Waadtländer Mitte-Staatsrätin ist erneut im Visier der Justiz. Noch ist offen, um welche Verdachtsmomente es sich handelt – Korruption ist es offenbar nicht.

nzz.description: Wenn die Temperaturen steigen, suchen die Menschen vor allem eines: Abkühlung. Diese Bilder zeigen Pools und Freibäder auf der ganzen Welt.

nzz.description: Die reichste Jungunternehmerin der Schweiz, Alexandra Lüönd, erzählt im Gespräch, warum das Geschäft mit Botox und Co. boomt, was ihr Ehrgeiz mit ihrer Kindheit zu tun hat und wann eine Frau ihr Geld besser für einen Scheidungsanwalt als für eine Schönheits-OP ausgeben sollte.

spiegel.title: Venedig: Bürgermeister Simone Venturini will Tageseintritt auf bis zu 50 Euro erhöhen
spiegel.description: Wenn Touristen einen Tag Venedig besuchen möchten, zahlen sie bereits Eintritt. Nun könnte sich der Preis verzehnfachen – zumindest, wenn es nach dem neuen Bürgermeister geht. Kritiker bezweifeln die Wirkung der Gebühr.

spiegel.title: Renningen: Ermittler finden Babyleiche auf Suche nach vermisstem Säugling
spiegel.description: Während der Suchaktion nach einem drei Monate alten Säugling in Renningen ist die Leiche eines Babys gefunden worden. Die Identifizierung dauert laut Polizei an.

spiegel.title: Eva Maria Michelmann: Auswärtiges Amt erreicht Freilassung der in Syrien festgehaltenen Deutschen
spiegel.description: Anfang des Jahres war Eva Maria Michelmann in Syrien verschwunden und zuletzt von der Regierung in Damaskus festgehalten worden. Nun hat das Auswärtige Amt nach Informationen des SPIEGEL ihre Freilassung erreicht.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM heute: Das sollten Sie vor den Spielen am Abend und in der Nacht wissen
spiegel.description: Wie geht’s weiter für Rekordweltmeister Brasilien? Die Seleção ist nach dem schwachen WM-Auftakt unter Druck. Gleiches gilt für die Türkei. Die USA wollen einen großen Schritt in Richtung K.-o.-Phase machen. Das müssen Sie wissen.

spiegel.description: Als sie eine tote Ameise untersuchten, machten Forschende aus Malaysia eine besondere Entdeckung: einen Hyperparasiten.

spiegel.title: Sommersonnenwende: Warum der späteste Sonnenuntergang erst danach kommt
spiegel.description: Der 21. Juni ist der längste Tag des Jahres. Doch der früheste Sonnenaufgang und der späteste Sonnenuntergang fallen auf ein anderes Datum. Dafür gibt es zwei Gründe.

spiegel.title: Schorndorf: Kleinkind starb im Auto nach Hitzeschlag
spiegel.description: Eine 44-jährige Mutter hatte ihre etwa 20 Monate alte Tochter stundenlang im Auto vergessen. Die Obduktion hat nun ergeben: Das Kleinkind erlitt einen Hitzschlag.

spiegel.description: Donald Trump lästert bei einem italienischen Fernsehsender über seine ehemalige Verbündete Giorgia Meloni. Die Regierung in Rom sieht sich brüskiert, der Außenminister sagt einen US-Besuch ab.

spiegel.title: Angelina Jolie: Warum sich ihr neuer Film für sie so persönlich anfühlt
spiegel.description: Ihre Mutter ist an Brustkrebs gestorben, sie selbst hat sich vorsorglich einer Mastektomie unterzogen. Nun spielt Angelina Jolie eine betroffene Frau und erzählt, wie verletzlich sie sich dabei gefühlt habe.

spiegel.title: Israel und Hisbollah-Miliz beschließen Waffenruhe
spiegel.description: Die Kämpfe zwischen der israelischen Armee und der Hisbollah sind in den vergangenen Tagen immer wieder aufgeflammt. Nun haben sich beide Seiten offenbar vorerst auf ein Ende der Angriffe verständigt.

spiegel.title: USA: Grippeausbruch auf Militärbasis – zwei Monate nach Streichung der verpflichtenden Impfung
spiegel.description: Vor wenigen Wochen erst hat das Pentagon die Impfvorgaben für seine Streitkräfte aufgeweicht. Nun sollen etwa 160 Soldaten auf einem Stützpunkt an Grippe erkrankt sein. Die Lockerung wurde zuvor kritisiert.

spiegel.description: Trumps Plan für einen Irandeal empört seine eigene Partei. Vor allem der 300-Milliarden-Dollar-Fonds stößt bei vielen auf Widerstand. Der US-Präsident sichert sich selbst ab – und schickt seinen Vize Vance vor.

spiegel.title: Forgotten-Baby-Syndrom: Wieso Menschen ihr Baby im Auto vergessen - und was Sie tun können
spiegel.description: Ein Auto in der Sonne, ein Kind auf dem Rücksitz – und ein fataler Kurzschluss im Gehirn: Immer wieder vergessen Eltern ihr Baby im Auto, wie jetzt im baden-württembergischen Schorndorf. Was sagen Experten? Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Mönchengladbach: 18 Jahre alte Frau an Tankstelle von Polizei angeschossen
spiegel.description: An einer Tankstelle in Mönchengladbach ist es zu einem größeren Polizeieinsatz gekommen. Dabei wurde eine junge Frau verletzt. Sie soll ein Messer bei sich gehabt haben.

spiegel.title: Rostock: AfD-Abgeordneter berichtet von nächtlichem Angriff mit "spitzem Gegenstand"
spiegel.description: Der Rostocker Landtagsabgeordnete Michael Meister wurde nach eigenen Angaben Opfer einer Attacke. Die Polizei ermittelt wegen versuchten Mordes und sucht Zeugen.

Radboud researcher Stephan Mols can often be found at the excavation site. "The new finds show that the Romans did not regard this city as a backwater. The buildings were even larger and more imposing than we had previously thought."

phys-org.title: Powerful seismic waves from Japan's 2011 earthquake struck Earth's core and bounced back up, moving the island eastward
phys-org.description: In 2011, Japan reeled from the effects of a devastating magnitude 9.0 earthquake. But unnoticed in the chaos resulting from the quake, its major aftershocks and the tsunami it caused, something strange happened. About 16 minutes after the earthquake, but before the aftershocks hit, Japan's GPS stations registered an eastward lurch—across the entire country—but unconnected to any specific quake or aftershock.

phys-org.title: Student makes first recorded sighting of a microwhip scorpion in the Daintree Rainforest
phys-org.description: A James Cook University Ph.D. student's late-night solo survey has led to the first recorded sighting of a microwhip scorpion in the Daintree Rainforest. JCU entomologist and taxonomist Matthew Connors works at the university's Daintree Rainforest Observatory as a demonstrator and rainforest tour guide for visiting groups.

phys-org.title: Small forest fragments can protect more birds when the surrounding landscape is more helpful
phys-org.description: Larger areas contain more species. This is one of the most ironclad laws of ecology, which explains why large natural areas usually receive higher priority in conservation strategies. In fragmented landscapes, this logic has also led small forest fragments to be seen as environments of lower value for biodiversity.

phys-org.title: Men make up less than 18% of Australian primary school teachers. Is this a problem?
phys-org.description: This week, a group of Australian primary school principals called for more male primary school teachers, saying boys needed more "male role models."

phys-org.title: Microbes destroyed an ancient pterosaur's wingbone, then preserved it for 100 million years
phys-org.description: More than 100 million years ago, a flying reptile called a pterosaur flew over the oceans hunting squid and fish.

phys-org.title: New Zealand scientists working on 'R' win major global award
phys-org.description: Scientists working on the revolutionary 'R' programming language invented at the University of Auckland have won a top award intended to be a Nobel Prize for statisticians.

phys-org.title: New research finds major gaps between EU anti-deforestation rules and realities on the ground in Brazil
phys-org.description: The U.K. could face significant challenges if it follows the European Union's lead and introduces tougher restrictions on imports linked to deforestation, according to new research from The University of Manchester. The study examines how the EU's landmark Regulation on Deforestation-Free Products (EUDR) is likely to work in practice in Brazil's beef sector, which is one of the world's largest sources of beef exports and a major driver of tropical deforestation.

phys-org.title: Desert field test with NASA advanced rover prototype
phys-org.description: A prototype four-wheel rover developed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory with advanced mobility and robotic autonomy capabilities trundled across the Colorado Desert near Plaster City, California, during a field test in March 2026. Called ERNEST (Exploration Rover for Navigating Extreme Sloped Terrain), the rover served here as a test bed for autonomy software developed for a potential lunar mission requiring higher speeds and much greater mileage than can be achieved with current planeta

phys-org.title: Five phases of localization physics observed in a single quantum system
phys-org.description: Physicists in China have observed five phases in localization physics within a single quantum system. Using an advanced photonic platform, the team, led by Yucheng Wang and Jingyun Fan at the Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, has demonstrated that localization physics is likely far richer than physicists anticipated. Their results have been published in Physical Review Letters.

phys-org.title: NASA mission to study space weather impacts of Earth's atmosphere
phys-org.description: NASA selected a mission concept to research how space weather and dynamics within Earth's atmosphere influence the space environment and help improve prediction capabilities for impacts on crucial technology, such as GPS and low Earth orbit satellites, as well as astronauts in space.

phys-org.title: Deadly Philippines quake turns seabed into shore
phys-org.description: Arsenio Butil Jr. fell to his knees and began to pray when last week's deadly 7.8-magnitude earthquake began shaking his home on the coast of the southern Philippines.

phys-org.title: Palm oil, coconut and soybean drive more species extinction than previously thought
phys-org.description: Oils from crops such as coconut, palm oil and soybean are used in a range of applications, from cosmetics and makeup to margarine and spreads, and from medicines to animal feed. These oil crops, as they are known, are increasingly consumed and cultivated. This has an impact on the environment. But what exactly is that impact?

phys-org.title: Molecular simulations uncover why water nanodrops spread thin on hydrophilic surfaces
phys-org.description: Why does water roll off a duck's back but spread on clean glass? For macroscopic (millimeter-scale) drops, this behavior can be explained using continuum theory. However, when nanoscale (10–9 mm) droplets spread on surfaces, a force called line tension becomes relevant and mysteriously changes sign. Questions about the nature of this force and its relevance to water's interaction with surfaces have remained unanswered.

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.19494v1 Announce Type: new

arxiv-ai.title: ITNet: A Learnable Integral Transform That Subsumes Convolution, Attention, and Recurrence
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.19538v1 Announce Type: new

We show that this fragmentation reflects not a fundamental diversity in how signals should be processed, but rather incomplete views of a single underlying mathematical object: a learnable integral transform.

arxiv-ai.description:

new-sci.title: Can prebiotics, probiotics or postbiotics help your ageing microbiome?
new-sci.description: The disruption of your gut microbiome is a major consequence, and possible cause, of ageing. Columnist Graham Lawton looks into recent trials examining whether it can be replenished through diet and prebiotics, probiotics or postbiotics

new-sci.title: Remarkable fossils rewrite the story of how animals conquered the land
new-sci.description: Palaeontologists have found new evidence that the early ancestors of amphibians, reptiles and mammals did not have a larval stage with external gills like modern frogs or salamanders

new-sci.title: Almost the whole of Japan moved eastward after 2011 earthquake
new-sci.description: An extremely unusual tectonic movement took place 15 minutes after the Tohoku earthquake in 2011, causing almost the whole of Japan to move 5 millimetres to the east

new-sci.title: A quantum state that lasts forever may finally be within our grasp
new-sci.description: Defying the laws of thermodynamics, experiments are beginning to show that a quantum state that is frozen forever might not be impossible. If we can tame it, it could unlock whole new types of matter

new-sci.title: Carl Sagan's The Demon-Haunted World is still supremely relevant today
new-sci.description: Beautifully written, this guide to distinguishing between truth, misinformation and lies, first published in 1995, remains an essential read for anyone who considers themselves a critical thinker, says Leah Crane

new-sci.title: Complex life on Earth may last 500 million years longer than expected
new-sci.description: As the sun expands over the coming billions of years, Earth will become inhospitable to any life more complex than a microbe – but that might take longer than we thought

new-sci.title: New Scientist recommends an excellent look at the future of work
new-sci.description: Sarah O'Connor's We Are Not Machines explores how we are contorting ourselves to fit AI into our working lives – and what to do about it, finds Tom Knowles

new-sci.title: Ancient monument marked summer solstice centuries before Stonehenge
new-sci.description: Archaeologists have discovered traces of a wooden structure built 5000 years ago, 5 kilometres from Stonehenge, which appears to have been an even older monument for marking the summer solstice

new-sci.title: Cervical cancer deaths have plummeted thanks to HPV vaccine
new-sci.description: We already know the vaccine against human papillomavirus, or HPV, greatly reduces infections and cases of cervical cancer, and now we have the first evidence it prevents deaths too

new-sci.title: Chilling the body with drugs could limit brain damage from stroke
new-sci.description: Putting brain cells into a hibernation-like state via drugs that cool down core body temperature may help to preserve them following a stroke

new-sci.title: Oldest known plague outbreak killed hunter-gatherer children
new-sci.description: DNA evidence shows that plague bacteria devastated a community in Siberia more than 5000 years ago, challenging the idea that there were no major disease outbreaks before the advent of farming and large settlements

new-sci.title: Pigeons lock their eyes in place when they are flying
new-sci.description: Bird-mounted headsets and backpacks have revealed the surprising things pigeons do with their eyes when on the wing

new-sci.title: Our brains have their first thoughts surprisingly early in life
new-sci.description: By the time we’re born, our brains have all the hardware in place to form thoughts, and possibly even some conscious awareness

new-sci.title: Autism and ADHD are on the rise due to widening diagnostic criteria
new-sci.description: A study of 140,000 people suggests that a broadening of the diagnostic criteria for autism and ADHD explains the sharp rise in diagnoses, but that doesn't mean too many people are being told they are autistic or have ADHD

new-sci.title: Autism may have two distinct subtypes that vary by brain activity
new-sci.description: Evidence is mounting that there are distinct subtypes of autism, and now, scientists have found that the condition can vary according to the strength of people's brain connections

new-sci.title: The secrets to keeping your brain sharp in old age
new-sci.description: Neuroscientist Emily Rogalski studies superagers – people in their 80s or 90s with unusually keen memories, whose lifestyles suggest ways to slow cognitive decline

new-sci.title: Walking shark found in Papua New Guinea is new to science
new-sci.description: Hemiscyllium dudgeonae is the tenth recorded species of walking shark, which use their pectoral fins to move across reef flats, and its limited range means it may be at high risk of extinction

new-sci.title: Sperm have been made magnetic to allow IVF inside the body
new-sci.description: IVF could be done inside the body using a revolutionary technique that reduces the invasiveness of the traditional fertility treatment

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Reversing Brexit Is Labour’s Best Hope
proj-syn.description: When it comes to the relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union, political expediency and economic logic both point in the same direction. A majority of British voters now believe that Brexit was a mistake, and they are looking for a leader who will put the issue back on the national agenda.

proj-syn.title: Global Health Reform Must Bolster Innovation
proj-syn.description: As funding falls for global public health, calls for a country-led system have grown louder. Such reforms are necessary, but they must not come at the expense of new vaccines, medicines, and diagnostics, which can be delivered by strengthening mechanisms—such as product development partnerships—that already work.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.

proj-syn.title: White House Fight Night
proj-syn.description: The venue on the South Lawn for UFC Freedom 250 was built, approved, lit, filmed, defended, watched, and enjoyed as part of a celebration of freedom. President Donald Trump’s chosen object to represent that celebration was a cage.

proj-syn.title: The US-Iran Agreement Is a First Step
proj-syn.description: While the recently announced US-Iranian memorandum of understanding is certainly good news, it is not definitive. The path from a statement of diplomatic intent to a fully restored, non-inflationary energy supply chain is fraught with political, technical, and physical risks.

proj-syn.title: Developing-Country Risk Is Being Mispriced
proj-syn.description: When investors say there are no “bankable” projects in developing economies, they are typically referring less to project quality than to the cost of capital. But the assumptions driving up risk premia are not supported by the evidence, and until this changes, the misallocation of capital will continue to undermine development.

proj-syn.title: The Fed Has Been Honest and Stupid
proj-syn.description: It would be easy—and a mistake—to blame the US Federal Reserve’s many blunders on corrupt bureaucrats or imagined conspiracies. The truth of the matter is that the central bank relies on an outdated regional map and lagging indicators that no longer tell the whole story, while battling macroeconomic blazes that politicians stoke.

proj-syn.title: A New Framework for Climate Displacement
proj-syn.description: Global warming is already uprooting communities and impoverishing people who remain in vulnerable areas—a crisis that is often overshadowed by the focus on decarbonization. But the Global Climate Mobility Principles offer policymakers a framework for ensuring that these individuals maintain their agency and rights.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Is All About Lebanon Now
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump says that he "calls the shots" on negotiating with Iran, and Israel has no choice but to submit to a deal that undermines its security interests. But a deal that makes Trump the protector of Lebanon—and, by extension, Iran-backed Hezbollah—could put the US and Israel on a collision course.

proj-syn.title: Every British Prime Minister’s Nightmare
proj-syn.description: The true nature of Britain’s “special relationship” with the United States has far more to do with American financiers’ willingness to keep borrowing to purchase British government debt than with history, culture, or Britain’s defense needs. Every UK Prime Minister must bear this burden, which is rapidly becoming unsustainable.
